title: The Sânkhya Aphorisms of Kapila
dateDisplay: c. 4th–6th century CE (the aphorisms themselves are older)
attributionNote: The aphorisms are traditionally ascribed to Kapila, the legendary founder of Sankhya. The surviving sutra collection is a later compilation, and the text translated here carries an anonymous commentary printed with it.
description: The Sânkhya Aphorisms set out the classical Sankhya system in six books: the existence and plurality of the selves, the three constituents of nature, the emergence of the world from unmanifest nature, the means of knowledge, the refutation of rival views, and the isolation of the self that is liberation. Ballantyne's translation presents the sutras with the commentary that explains them.
historicalContext: Sankhya is one of the oldest of the six Hindu philosophical systems; its classical formulation is the Sankhya-karika of Ishvarakrishna, while the sutras attributed to Kapila represent a later, more scholastic stage. James R. Ballantyne's translation was first published in 1852 and revised for the third edition of 1885.
availabilityNote: Complete. All six books of Ballantyne's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one book per chapter. The advertisement and preface of the printed volume are not part of the work.
